question: diffusion models for video generation

2112.10752.caption: The figure presents a comparison of image synthesis quality across three models (ours, DALL-E, and VQGAN) using different spatial downsampling factors ($f$). It displays a grid of input images alongside reconstructed/generated outputs, accompanied by text labels indicating the downsampling factor, PSNR, and R-FID for each method. The figure conveys that the proposed model achieves higher image quality (higher PSNR and lower R-FID) by using a less aggressive downsampling factor.

2006.11239.caption: The figure displays two sets of image grids: a 2x2 grid of high-resolution human faces on the left and a large 10x10 grid of diverse, low-resolution objects (such as animals, vehicles, and landscapes) on the right. It conveys the quality and variety of images generated by the model on the CelebA-HQ and CIFAR-10 datasets.

2103.00020.caption: The figure illustrates the CLIP framework through three panels: (1) a contrastive pre-training stage showing an image and text being processed by respective encoders to produce a matrix of similarity scores between $N$ image and $N$ text embeddings; (2) the creation of a dataset classifier by passing label texts through a text encoder; and (3) zero-shot prediction where an image embedding is compared against the text embeddings of potential labels. The diagram uses boxes for data inputs and encoders, and arrows to represent the flow of information toward a similarity matrix.

2010.02502.caption: The figure displays two sequences of directed nodes, $x_3$ through $x_0$, connected by arrows to represent probabilistic dependencies. The left model shows a Markovian chain where each node $x_t$ depends only on $x_{t+1}$ (labeled $p_\theta$) or $x_{t-1}$ (labeled $q(x_t|x_{t+1})$), while the right model shows a non-Markovian process where $x_t$ depends on all subsequent states $x_{t+1}, \dots, x_0$ via dashed arrows. The figure conveys the structural difference between standard diffusion inference models and the proposed non-Markovian DDIM inference models.

2209.14792.caption: Figure 1 displays four rows of image sequences, labeled (a) through (d), representing video frames generated from text prompts. Each row illustrates a different visual concept—a flying superhero dog, a pile of books by a window, a dancing robot, and running unicorns—to demonstrate the model's ability to produce coherent motion and high-quality video generation.

2210.02303.caption: The figure displays a grid of eight video frames showing autumn leaves falling onto a blue lake. The sequence progresses from leaves scattered randomly on the water to leaves settling into a pattern that spells out the text "IMAGEN VIDEO."

2204.03458.caption: The figure depicts a 3D U-Net architecture consisting of a sequence of colored rectangular blocks connected by arrows, representing a downsampling path followed by an upsampling path. The blocks are labeled with dimensions in the format of frames $\times$ height $\times$ width $\times$ channels, and curved arrows indicate concatenation skip connections from the downsampling blocks to the corresponding upsampling blocks. The diagram conveys the hierarchical structure of the model, showing how spatial resolution is reduced through $K$ blocks and subsequently restored.

2304.08818.caption: The figure displays two rows of video frame sequences generated from text prompts. The top row shows three examples of text-to-video generation—a horse in a Van Gogh style, a dog in VR goggles, and a train in a fantasy landscape—while the bottom row shows a sequence of high-resolution real driving scenes.

2604.15911.caption: The figure consists of three bar charts showing the distribution and trends of accelerated sampling algorithms. The left chart shows the proportion of literature across different categories, with "Step Distillation" being the largest at 41.2%; the middle chart displays the annual publication count for various specific algorithms from 2022 to 2026; and the right chart compares the growth in paper counts for "only video," "only image," and "both" tasks over the same period.

2605.17248.caption: The figure illustrates the basic architecture of image-to-video (I2V) diffusion models through a series of interconnected blocks and data flow arrows. It depicts a spatiotemporal generative backbone composed of spatial blocks, temporal blocks, and cross-attention mechanisms that process latent and conditioning encodings (from text, audio, or motion inputs) alongside VAE-encoded image inputs. The diagram conveys how various conditioning signals and time embeddings are integrated into the generative process to produce video sequences.

2603.17398.caption: The figure illustrates a pipeline for video generation, showing the flow from Pixel Space (containing $x$ and $\hat{x}$) through an encoder $\mathcal{E}$ into a Latent Space. Within the Latent Space, a Diffusion Process operates on latents $z_0$ and $z_\tau$, while a Denoising U-Net—composed of Up, Mid, and Down Blocks—processes these latents using spatial transformers and temporal attention layers (adaptive or global) conditioned by a Text Encoder.

2602.02092.caption: Figure 1 displays a grid of three rows, each containing a sequence of six images showing the temporal progression of a video. The rows depict a penguin walking on a beach, a person riding a horse, and a person walking in a landscape, illustrating the model's ability to generate subsequent video frames from an initial input image.

2603.09721.caption: The figure presents a block diagram of the FrameDiT architecture, illustrating three different attention mechanisms: (a) a local factorized approach with standard attention, (b) a global approach using Matrix Attention, and (c) a hybrid approach combining both. Each sub-figure uses colored boxes to represent architectural components like AdaLN, MLP, and Scale layers, connected by arrows to show the data flow from input video frames through the transformer blocks.
